intro_script: Welcome to the Robotics News Digest for November 14, 2026. Today we cover the drone revolution, major investment in drone manufacturing, and exciting advancements in human motion for robots.

items.title: Wing invests $125 million in US drone manufacturing to support nationwide expansion
items.summary: Wing is investing up to $125 million over two years in US drone manufacturing to support nationwide expansion. This investment includes a new 15,000-square-foot facility in Fort Worth, Texas, which will generate up to 100 jobs. The expansion aims to extend drone delivery services to over 40 million Americans across nearly 20 US markets by 2027. Wing has already completed over one million residential deliveries in the United States this year. This manufacturing expansion supports the growth of autonomous aerial delivery amid evolving US aviation regulations.

items.summary: Zipline raised $1.5 billion to expand its nationwide drone delivery network, aiming to address limitations of ground delivery. Partnerships with companies like Walmart and Uber are driving growth, with a goal to achieve one million deliveries per day by 2029. Zipline's service is valued for its speed, convenience, and reduced traffic impact, demonstrated by rapid delivery times. The company is continuously improving its technology, including quieter and more efficient aircraft, and has a successful track record in autonomous delivery.

items.title: Adapt Human Motion for Robots with NVIDIA SOMA Retargeter
items.summary: NVIDIA SOMA Retargeter adapts human motion data to humanoid robots by using the shared SOMA skeleton representation. It scales motion targets, solves inverse kinematics using NVIDIA Warp, and applies post-processing like foot-plant adjustment to fit robot proportions. Developers can source motion from various datasets or generative models and export retargeted trajectories for policy training workflows. Tools like the Robot Configurator allow for refining robot configurations and optimizing inverse-kinematics priorities for smoother motion. The system enables the adaptation of human movement to teach humanoid robots locomotion and for simulation evaluation.

The system scales motion targets, resolves inverse kinematics through NVIDIA Warp, and incorporates post-processing such as foot-plant adjustment to align with robot proportions. Developers can source motion from diverse datasets or generative models to export retargeted trajectories for policy training workflows. Tools like the Robot Configurator facilitate the refinement of robot configurations and the optimization of inverse-kinematics priorities for smoother motion. This mechanism enables the adaptation of human movement to teach humanoid robots locomotion and for simulation evaluation. This advancement facilitates the training of sophisticated humanoid robotics systems through realistic motion transfer.

items.title: Why Build a Humanoid Robot From the Sensor Up? The Thinking Behind GENTO’s CoRL 2026 Debut
items.summary: GENTO's humanoid robot development stems from incorporating MEMS torque sensors within each joint, which dictate robot reactions to contact. Tianji Intelligence developed these sensors and built a five-tier system: sensors, integrated joint modules, dual arms, whole-body systems, and a dexterous hand. The system utilizes high-sensitivity sensors capable of measuring torque as low as 0.02 N·m for accurate force control. This approach enabled demonstrations, such as the TIANJI Marvin Pro platform, used in NVIDIA's GR00T 2 open-world action model. The company's philosophy centers on achieving gentle interaction by starting with precise joint torque readings.

Tianji Intelligence developed a five-tier system encompassing sensors, integrated joint modules, dual arms, whole-body systems, and a dexterous hand. This system employs high-sensitivity sensors capable of measuring torque as low as 0.02 Newton-meters to achieve accurate force control. This methodology enabled demonstrations on platforms such as the TIANJI Marvin Pro system utilized in NVIDIA's GR00T open-world action model, emphasizing the goal of achieving gentle interaction through precise joint torque readings. This approach signals a focus on fine-grained physical interaction in future robotics development.

items.title: Six AGIBOT G2 Robots Complete 1,730 Tasks in 24-Hour Shanghai Convenience Store Trial
items.summary: Six AGIBOT G2 robots completed 1,730 tasks over a 24-hour trial in a Shanghai convenience store, performing duties like customer assistance and restocking. The trial tested embodied AI's ability to operate effectively in a live, changing retail environment, going beyond controlled demonstrations. The robots utilized real-time visual information to adapt to dynamic conditions, such as repositioning merchandise and cleaning spills. The Genie Master framework coordinated the robots, allowing them to learn from operational experiences to improve future performance. AGIBOT plans to continue real-world testing to enhance the reliability and adaptability of its robotic systems.

The operation relied on the robots utilizing real-time visual information to adjust to shifting conditions, enabling actions such as repositioning merchandise and managing liquid spills. items.title: Automated Warehouses: Why Safety Infrastructure Matters More Than Ever
items.summary: Increased automation in warehouses necessitates robust safety infrastructure to manage the risks from moving machinery and personnel. Effective safety measures are crucial for preventing collisions and ensuring smooth operations in this complex environment. Clear traffic routes and floor markings are essential to separate pedestrian and automated vehicle paths. Flooring must withstand heavy traffic and include slip-resistant finishes to prevent hazards. Overall safety requires a combination of intelligent technology and physical protection, supported by regular assessments.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Automated Warehouses: Why Safety Infrastructure Matters More Than Ever". This story examines the necessity of robust safety infrastructure in increasingly automated warehouse environments to manage risks from moving machinery and personnel. Effective safety measures are crucial for preventing collisions and ensuring smooth operations in this complex setting. The implementation of effective safety measures requires clearly defined traffic routes and floor markings to delineate paths for pedestrians and automated vehicles. Furthermore, warehouse flooring must possess the capacity to endure heavy traffic and incorporate slip-resistant finishes to mitigate potential hazards. Comprehensive safety necessitates an integration of intelligent technology and physical protection, supported by routine safety assessments. This focus on integrated physical and technological safety protocols indicates a growing mandate for safety-by-design principles across the industrial automation sector.

items.title: Neura Robotics partners with E.ON to bring humanoid robots to energy infrastructure
items.summary: Neura Robotics, E.ON, and enviaM are partnering to develop physical AI applications for electricity networks using intelligent robots. The collaboration aims to use robots to inspect and monitor energy infrastructure and assist workers with physically demanding tasks. Training will occur at a specialized facility using multimodal AI and real-world data to develop robotic skills. A potential application involves using humanoid robots to navigate existing infrastructure for inspection and maintenance support. Initial practical trials are scheduled to begin in 2027 with Mitnetz Strom as the pilot partner.

items.title: Gecko Robotics unveils faster Raptor inspection robot, with ADNOC as first customer
items.summary: Gecko Robotics introduced Raptor, a next-generation industrial inspection robot designed for significantly faster data collection on critical infrastructure. Raptor can inspect pipelines and tanks, gathering data three to five times faster than existing robots. It features improved mobility, allowing it to navigate complex spaces and perform three-point turns. The robot can collect millions of data points, which are analyzed using Gecko's AI software. ADNOC in the UAE is the first customer, with plans for international installations.

items.title: Video Friday: NASA PROMISEs a New Moon Rover
items.summary: NASA plans to send a nuclear-powered rover named PROMISE to the Moon's South Pole as a key mission for the Moon Base Program. This rover will be constructed primarily from components developed for the Mars rovers, Curiosity and Perseverance. A demonstration of automated in-space assembly was achieved by a Caltech payload building a truss structure in orbit. Various robotics applications are being explored, including using mobile robots for security and solving complex multi-agent planning problems in manufacturing. Further developments are occurring in humanoid robotics, autonomous navigation, and AI in motion.

items.title: Queue introduces robotic pharmacy kiosk that fills prescriptions in 30 seconds
items.summary: Queue has introduced an autonomous robotic pharmacy kiosk capable of filling, verifying, and labeling prescriptions in about 30 seconds. The system can handle 340 medications and uses machine vision for verification, requiring less than a day for installation without patient membership fees. The kiosk will target community pharmacies, retail chains, and clinics, aiming to dispense medications without a traditional storefront. The process involves a patient pickup code, automated medication preparation, and software handling insurance and payment. This technology aims to improve medication access and reduce pharmacy closures, addressing disparities in healthcare access.

items.title: Welcome, AIRoA-0!
items.summary: The AIRoA-0 robot foundation model originates from Japan's AI Robot Association, supported by the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry. It falls into the vision-language action model category, focusing on connecting AI research with robot control. The model was trained using over 16,000 hours of human recordings collected via YUBI, a handheld gripper developed with Toyota. The project emphasizes an alternative method for building robot training datasets that minimizes the need for extensive robot operation. The model is classified as developing, and its research focus is on demonstration collection costs and open distribution.

items.title: ASUS Gallop humanoid learns to pack motherboard accessories
items.summary: ASUS is training its Gallop humanoid to pack motherboard accessories in a group electronics manufacturing services factory. The task involves handling 15 varied accessories with small, thin, and flexible plastic packaging. Gallop learns through worker demonstrations, simulation, and practice with the actual parts. The objective is to achieve a 99.5 percent task success rate within 20 seconds for the factory test. ASUS aims for commercial availability in the second half of 2028, following customer pilot programs in 2027.

The training process involved worker demonstrations, simulation, and practical practice using the actual components. The humanoid handled fifteen varied accessories, which utilized small, thin, and flexible plastic packaging materials. This was accomplished through iterative learning methodologies within the factory setting. ASUS plans for commercial availability in the second half of twenty twenty-eight, succeeding prior customer pilot programs in twenty twenty-seven. This development signals advancements in dexterous manipulation for robotic systems in manufacturing environments.

items.title: Apple HALO reaches reported 91% success on Unitree G1 tests
items.summary: Apple's HALO humanoid control system achieved a 91% success rate across 360 single-task trials on a Unitree G1 in six unseen real environments. This evaluation tested tasks like obstacle navigation and interaction with furniture in environments that were not pre-scanned. Training involved 300 hours of simulated motion across virtual rooms with randomized visual variations. The system operates offline using a three-level architecture where a task interpreter generates movement instructions, which are then executed by a motion-tracking layer. The research sought to determine if synthetic experience transfers effectively to unfamiliar physical spaces.
items.audio_script: From Humanoid.guide, Apple HALO reaches reported 91% success on Unitree G1 tests. This report details an evaluation of the Apple HALO humanoid control system demonstrating a ninety-one percent success rate across three hundred sixty single-task trials conducted on a Unitree G1 in six different, unseen real environments. The testing involved thirty hundred hours of simulated motion across virtual rooms featuring randomized visual variations to facilitate training. The system operates through a three-level architecture where a task interpreter generates movement instructions which are subsequently executed by a motion-tracking layer, with the research aiming to assess the transfer of synthetic experience to unfamiliar physical spaces. This finding indicates progress in enabling artificial general intelligence to operate effectively in unpredictable physical settings.

items.title: Expoline completes international logistics project for humanoid robots
items.summary: Expoline, a South Korean logistics specialist, completed a multimodal project for a global physical AI robotics company involving humanoid robots. The company managed the transportation of sensitive robotic equipment from China to South Korea for the 2026 Seoul AI Robot Show. Expoline handled customs clearance, exhibition booth delivery, and the safe return shipment to China, utilizing an air import and ocean return strategy. This complex operation involved specialized handling and adherence to ATA Carnet regulations without customs delays. The successful execution of these projects highlights Expoline's expertise in advanced robotics logistics and international exhibition support.

items.title: NEXCOM expands RoboWIZ robotics platform with new technology partners
items.summary: NEXCOM expanded its RoboWIZ platform by partnering with technology providers like RealSense, Stereolabs, Synapticon, and Reynolds & Moore. RoboWIZ creates an open ecosystem to simplify integrating AI, motion control, perception, and safety technologies into robotic systems. The platform allows developers to combine components from various suppliers rather than being restricted to a single hardware architecture. It encompasses five areas: AI core control, functional safety, visual perception, real-time control, and actuation. This modular approach aims to reduce development and integration complexity for diverse robot applications.

items.title: Humble Robotics raises $51 million to expand autonomous electric freight operations
items.summary: Humble Robotics secured $51 million in Series A funding, bringing its total funding to $75 million, to expand autonomous electric freight operations. The company focuses on a unified autonomous, electric platform enabling seamless dock-to-dock transport between various logistics points. Humble's current focus is on regional freight routes under 250 miles, representing a major market opportunity. The new funding will support customer pilots, testing, and the expansion of their modular vehicle platform. Humble aims to make autonomous freight safer, more reliable, and more scalable for the economy.

items.title: How Rhoda AI is using video data to create generalized AI models for robots
items.summary: Rhoda AI pretrains models on internet-scale video to build a strong understanding of motion, physics, and physical interaction for robotics. The company's Direct Video Action (DVA) model combines video history and language tokens to predict future video frames and convert those predictions into robot actions. This process involves an observation, prediction, action execution, and a new observation loop for continuous learning. Using broad video data allows the models to generalize across different robot forms, and post-training with task-specific data refines the skills for real-world applications. Rhoda AI aims to use this generalized approach to advance robotics in manufacturing and logistics.
items.audio_script: From The Robot Report, "How Rhoda AI is using video data to create generalized AI models for robots". This report details how Rhoda AI pretrains models on internet-scale video to build a strong understanding of motion, physics, and physical interaction essential for robotics. The company's Direct Video Action model incorporates video history and language tokens to predict subsequent video frames and translate those predictions into executable robot actions through a cycle of observation, prediction, action execution, and a new observation loop for continuous learning. This generalized approach leverages broad video data to enable models to generalize across various robot forms before fine-tuning with task-specific data for practical applications in manufacturing and logistics. The development indicates a pathway toward more adaptable and capable robotic systems across industrial settings.
